newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WORLD BANK TALKS ON LESOTHO DAM FROZEN OVER UNREST.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK TALKS ON LESOTHO DAM FROZEN OVER UNREST.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn said on Friday talks with Lesotho on the second phase of the Highlands Water Project had been suspended because of political uncertainty.

"We've put about $100 million in phase one, there are negotiations going on currently about phase two, but with some disturbances now politically in Lesotho, which I don't think will turn us off the project in any sense, we're waiting for things to calm down before we continue the negotiations," he told a news conference in Cape Town.
The water project involves building dams and tunnels in Lesotho to change water flow from south to north so it will be diverted to South Africa's commercial and industrial hub in Gauteng province.
